ops.text:
ccx vcs ship is unrecoverable when a sibling worktree's bookmark sits on trunk's commit: two independent resolution steps, and only the first consumes --branch.

Hit while releasing binrun v0.3.1 (jj-colocated, own repo). A linked worktree's branch `release-v0.4.0` and `main` both pointed at commit 3056642. Ship refused twice, at two DIFFERENT steps:

  (1) no flag, trunk resolution:
      ccx: ship: cannot resolve the trunk bookmark from ["main" "release-v0.4.0"]; pass --branch naming one of them

  (2) WITH --branch main, i.e. the escape hatch (1) names, nearest-bookmark resolution:
      ccx: ship: multiple nearest bookmarks "main, release-v0.4.0"; pass --branch <name> to choose one

The defect is the shape, not either message alone. These are two separate lookups. `--branch main` satisfies gate 1 (trunk identity). Gate 2 — deciding which bookmark the commit appends to — re-derives its candidate set from the commit graph and never reads the flag. Its error then instructs the operator to pass `--branch <name>`: the exact flag that just succeeded at gate 1 and provably cannot help here. A documented escape hatch that clears one gate and cannot clear the next is worse than none, because it sends the reader in a circle with no in-tool way forward. Either gate 2 should honour --branch, or its message should name a remedy that can actually work (e.g. "delete or move the sibling bookmark").

Trigger is ordinary, not an edge case: ANY linked worktree whose branch sits on the same commit as trunk — i.e. any worktree cut off trunk that has not committed yet. That is the normal state of a fresh release or feature worktree. A fleet-wide daemonkit migration created several of these simultaneously, so it is easy to hit and confusing when hit.

Correct part, worth preserving: both refusals happened BEFORE any mutation. The working copy was untouched and nothing was left half-done. Only recoverability is broken, not safety.

Red/green bracket, verified rather than assumed. Before: `ccx vcs info` reported `branch  main release-v0.4.0` and resolved no trunk line at all; ship refused as above. After removing the worktree (git worktree remove --force), deleting the bookmark (jj bookmark delete release-v0.4.0) and git worktree prune: `ccx vcs info` reports `trunk  main`, and a no-op ship probe now reaches the empty-working-copy refusal — "ccx: ship: nothing to commit — did a prior ship already land 1d7bd9ad1bec ..." — which proves it cleared bookmark resolution and refused for the right reason, rather than merely failing differently.

Workaround used: manual jj path — uvx prek run --files <file> (so the hook gate still ran), then jj commit, jj bookmark set main -r @-, jj git push --bookmark main.

Adjacent but distinct from backlog item 706d5d1 (ship auto-tracking an untracked trunk bookmark): here both bookmarks are tracked and valid; the problem is ambiguity resolution plus a flag that only one of two gates honours.
